reasoning: Cross-section of corn ear showing distinctive pink to reddish-purple mold/discoloration throughout the cob tissues and between kernel rows. This pink-red coloration is the hallmark of Gibberella ear rot (Fusarium graminearum), which produces pinkish-red mycelium that colonizes the cob pith and spreads between kernels. Diplodia (white-gray) and Aspergillus (olive-green) are ruled out by color. Fusarium ear rot is possible but typically manifests as pink-white starburst on individual kernels rather than systemic cob discoloration.
